newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Mercosur nations plan new lending organization.
newsitem.headline: Mercosur nations plan new lending organization.

text.p: The four Mercosur partner countries and Bolivia have agreed to begin work on a new multilateral lending agency that would serve to finance trade and infrastructure projects in the region.

In a statement issued Tuesday at the XI Mercosur Council Meeting, the Finance and Planning ministers of Argentina, Brazil, Paraguay, Uruguay and Bolivia agreed to put together a working group that will define the framework of the new organization by mid 1997.
Asked in a news conference to explain the need of the new agency, Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said the bank would pool the resources of the five countries.
"I agree there is no point creating new state banks. The aim is to find funding for infrastructure projects in the region," he said.

The Mercosur statement said the new agency would be autonomous and structured like a bank. It said it would receive financing from outside the region, from multilateral lending agencies, public and private financial institutions.

"Its decision systems, capital structure, operational rules, credit facilities and functioning will be in line with the criteria currently in use by international financial agencies," the statement said.

The statement said the new agency will replace the FONPLATA, an already established financing organization which served the countries of the River Plate Basin but which has only played a limited role in the region.

The new lending agency is being proposed at a time in which most of the Mercosur countries are undergoing a dramatic restructuring of their financial sector and governments are busy closing loss-making state banks.
